Rashi on Gittin 60b:10:1.hebrew: במיזל כ"ע לא פליגי - אם אינן סוכרים את הנהר, אלא דולין והולכים והנהר מושך כפשטו, כ"ע לא פליגי שכל הרוצה לדלות ידלה:
Rashi on Gittin 60b:10:1.english: When [it] flows, everyone agrees - If they do not dam the river, but rather draw [water] continuously while the river flows along its natural course, everyone agrees that whoever wishes to draw [water] may draw.

Rashi on Gittin 60b:10:2.hebrew: כי פליגי במיסכר ואשקויי - שאין בו כדי לדלות כולן יחד, ורוצין העליונים לסוכרו שלא ירדו המים למטה, ולהמשיך הנהר דרך נגרים קטנים עד שישתו כל שדותיהן; ותחתונים מעכבין עליהם ואומרים: אלא א"כ נשקה אנחנו תחילה:
Rashi on Gittin 60b:10:2.english: When they disagree, [it is] regarding damming and irrigating - for there is not enough [water] in [the river] for all of them to draw at once, and the upper [field owners] want to dam it so that the water will not go down below, and to divert the river through small channels until all their fields are watered; and the lower [field owners] object to them, [saying: We will not allow it] unless we irrigate first.

Rashi on Gittin 60b:11:1.english: [The pit] closest to the irrigation channel - That is, the upper [upstream] one:

Rashi on Gittin 60b:11:2.hebrew: באמה המתהלכת ע"פ בורו - שמתמלא מאיליו כדרך הילוכו, ואין צריך לסכור הנהר:
Rashi on Gittin 60b:11:2.english: In [the case of] an irrigation channel that passes by the mouth of his pit - so that [the pit] fills on its own in the course of its flow, and there is no need to dam the river:

Rashi on Gittin 60b:12:1.hebrew: סכר מיסכר - פי בורך, שלא ירדו המים לתוכו, שממעט משיכת הנהר:
Rashi on Gittin 60b:12:1.english: Dam [it] - [dam] the mouth of your pit, so that the water does not descend into it, for [that] diminishes the flow of the river:

Rashi on Gittin 60b:12:2.hebrew: ואשקי בהנדזא - אוינטור"א, כפי מה שיעלה לך לדלות מן משיכת הנהר כמונו, כמו דמהנדזי להדדי בשחיטת חולין (דף מג.):
Rashi on Gittin 60b:12:2.english: And irrigate behindeza - [In Old French,] aventure [chance] — according to whatever comes up for you to draw from the flow of the river, just like us, similar to [the usage] "dimehandezei lahadadi" [they measure with one another] in Shechitat Chullin (43a):

Rashi on Gittin 60b:13:1.english: Whoever is stronger prevails - And he [Rav Huna bar Taḥalifa] does not hold that the halakha is in accordance with Shmuel in monetary cases:

Rashi on Gittin 60b:14:1.english: Master, seat me at a set time - May my master seat me to study at a fixed time:

Rashi on Gittin 60b:15:1.english: [The] lowermost [owners] drink first - and you are not permitted to dam it:

Rashi on Gittin 60b:16:2.english: Shanvata - The name of the river:

Rashi on Gittin 60b:16:3.hebrew: כרו ברישא דשנוותא ואהדרוה בשלהי נהרא - רצו להקיף את שדותיהן במי הנהר, וכרו מלמעלה לשדותיהן לצד ראש העליון של הנהר, והסיבו מקצתן סביב שדותיהן, ובסוף שדותיהן הסיבוהו עד שחזר ונפל לתוך הנהר (כזה):
Rashi on Gittin 60b:16:3.english: They dug at the head of the Shanvata [River] and returned it at the end of the river - They wanted to surround their fields with the water of the river, so they dug above their fields toward the upper end of the river, and diverted some of it around their fields, and at the end of their fields they diverted it [back] until it returned and flowed into the river (like this):

Rashi on Gittin 60b:16:4.hebrew: קא מתקיל לנהרין - נהר שלנו נתקל מפני שהסיבוהו, ואינו נמשך מהר, וצפין המים דרך שדותינו; שכן דרך הנהר המיסב — אין מימיו קלין לרוץ מפני העקמומית:
Rashi on Gittin 60b:16:4.english: It impedes our river - Our river is impeded because they diverted it, and it does not flow swiftly, and the water overflows across our fields; for such is the way of a winding river — its waters are not swift to run because of the curvature:

Rashi on Gittin 60b:16:5.hebrew: כרו בהדייהו טפי פורתא - העמיקו המים אצלכם בראש המסיבה, כדי שישטפו המים במרוצה:
Rashi on Gittin 60b:16:5.english: Dig a little more with them - Deepen the water [channel] on your side at the head of the diversion, so that the water will flow swiftly:

Rashi on Gittin 60b:16:6.hebrew: קא יבשי פירין - אם נעמיק, ייבשו חריצין שלנו; כשלא יתברכו מימי הנהר, יעמיקו המים ויחדל הלחלוחית, ולא ינבעו המים לחריצין שיש לנו:
Rashi on Gittin 60b:16:6.english: Our pits will become dry - If we dig deeper, our ditches will dry up; when the waters of the river are not abundant, the water will lie deep [below] and the moisture will cease, and the water will not seep into the ditches that we have:

Rashi on Gittin 60b:16:7.english: Pits - Like "a pit of fish" [i.e., a fishpond] (Ketubot 79a):

Rashi on Gittin 60b:16:8.english: He said to them - Abaye [said] to the residents of [Bei] Ḥarmakh:

Rashi on Gittin 60b:16:9.english: Remove yourselves - and dam up your diversion [channel]:

Rashi on Gittin 60b:17:1.english: Uzlei - Nets [made] of threads that have an interior [receptacle]:

Rashi on Gittin 60b:17:2.english: Oharei - [traps made] of reeds, [in Old French:] jonquières:

Rashi on Gittin 60b:1:1.hebrew: ופרשת שתויי יין - לפי שמאותו היום ואילך נאסרו, דהא בביאת אהל מועד תלה רחמנא:
Rashi on Gittin 60b:1:1.english: And the section of those intoxicated with wine - Because from that day onward they were prohibited, for the Merciful One made [the prohibition] dependent upon entering the Tent of Meeting:

Rashi on Gittin 60b:1:2.hebrew: ופרשת נרות - בהעלותך, לפי שבו ביום התחילו להדליק:
Rashi on Gittin 60b:1:2.english: And the section of the lamps - [This refers to the section of] Beha'alotekha (Numbers 8:1–4), because on that day they began to light [the Menorah]:

Rashi on Gittin 60b:1:3.hebrew: ופרשת פרה אדומה - לפי שביום המחרת נשרפה הפרה, להיות נטהרין לפסחיהן, וקודם לכן לא יכלו לעשותה, דבעינן: "והזה אל נכח פני אהל מועד" (במדבר י״ט:ד׳). והכי אמרינן במסכת מגילה ירושלמי: "באחד בניסן הוקם המשכן, ושני לו נשרפה הפרה":
Rashi on Gittin 60b:1:3.english: And the section of the red heifer - Because on the following day the [red] heifer was burned, so that they could become purified for their Passover offerings; and prior to that they could not perform [the rite], for we require: "and he shall sprinkle toward the front of the Tent of Meeting" (Numbers 19:4). And so we say in Tractate Megillah [of the] Jerusalem [Talmud]: "On the first of Nisan the Tabernacle was erected, and on the second [day] of it the [red] heifer was burned":

Rashi on Gittin 60b:2:1.hebrew: רוב בכתב - רוב התורה תלויה במדרש, שכתובה למידרש בכלל ופרט, וגזירה שוה, ושאר מדות שהתורה נדרשת בהן:
Rashi on Gittin 60b:2:1.english: The majority in writing - The majority of the Torah depends on [scriptural] exposition, as it is written to be expounded through generalization and specification, verbal analogy [gezeirah shavah], and the other [hermeneutic] principles by which the Torah is expounded:

Rashi on Gittin 60b:2:2.hebrew: ומיעוטה על פה - שאין רמז ללמוד לה בתורה, אלא למשה נאמר על פה:
Rashi on Gittin 60b:2:2.english: And its minority [was transmitted] orally - [meaning] that there is no allusion from which to learn it in the [Written] Torah; rather, it was stated to Moses orally:

Rashi on Gittin 60b:2:3.hebrew: כי על פי וגו' - על שבעל פה נכרת ברית, אלמא איהי הואי רובא:
Rashi on Gittin 60b:2:3.english: For on the basis of, etc. - The covenant was made on [the basis of] that which is oral, thus [indicating that] it is the majority:

Rashi on Gittin 60b:3:1.english: It is written, "Write for yourself" - Thus, [part of the Torah] was written:

Rashi on Gittin 60b:3:2.hebrew: וכתיב ע"פ - אלמא לא נכתבה:
Rashi on Gittin 60b:3:2.english: And it is written: “orally” [lit. “by mouth”] - Thus [we see that] it was not written:

Rashi on Gittin 60b:3:3.hebrew: אתמוהי מתמה - וכי רובי תורתי היה לי לכתוב להם? והלא באותה שכתבתי להם, "כמו זר נחשבו":
Rashi on Gittin 60b:3:3.english: [The verse] is expressing bewilderment - Should I have written for them the greater part of My Torah? Why, [even] with that [portion] which I wrote for them, "they were reckoned as strangers":

Rashi on Gittin 60b:4:1.hebrew: דברים - שאמרתי לך בכתב, אי אתה רשאי למוסרם לישראל על פה:
Rashi on Gittin 60b:4:1.english: Matters - [Those] that I said to you in writing, you are not permitted to transmit them to Israel orally:

Rashi on Gittin 60b:5:1.english: And matters that were [taught] orally you may not write them - From here you learn that the Talmud was not permitted to be written except because the Torah was being forgotten:

Rashi on Gittin 60b:7:1.english: If we say [that it is] because of respect - for the owner of the house:

Rashi on Gittin 60b:7:2.hebrew: והא שופר - של תקיעת ע"ש, דמעיקרא הוי בי רב יהודה, שהיה ראש ישיבה בפומבדיתא, ולבסוף כשנפטר ומלך רבה נתנוהו בביתו, ובתר רבה מלך רב יוסף, והדר מלך אביי, והדר מלך רבא. ורב שרירא גאון פירש בכתב תשובתו: שיפורא — שופר של נדבה, שהיו נותנין לתוכו נדבה השלוחה לבני הישיבה, כמו "י"ג שופרות היו במקדש" (שקלים דף ח):
Rashi on Gittin 60b:7:2.english: And [what about] the shofar - [This refers to the shofar] for blowing on Shabbat eve, which initially was in the house of Rav Yehuda, who was the head of the academy in Pumbedita; and afterward, when he passed away and Rabbah assumed leadership, they placed it in his house; and after Rabbah, Rav Yosef assumed leadership, and then Abaye assumed leadership, and then Rava assumed leadership. And Rav Sherira Gaon explained in his written responsum: Shippura [means] a charity shofar [chest], into which they would place donations sent for the members of the academy, just as [the Mishnah states]: "There were thirteen shofarot [horn-shaped chests] in the Temple" (Shekalim 8):

Rashi on Gittin 60b:8:1.hebrew: משום חשדא - הואיל והורגל העירוב בתוך אותו הבית, אם באת לשנות את מקומו, הנכנסין לאותו הבית ולא יראו שם את העירוב יחשדו את בני החצר שמטלטלין בלא עירוב:
Rashi on Gittin 60b:8:1.english: Because of suspicion - Since the eiruv had been customarily [placed] inside that house, if you were to change its location, those who enter that house and do not see the eiruv there will suspect the residents of the courtyard of carrying without an eiruv:

Rashi on Gittin 60b:9:1.english: People of the river - [Owners of] fields that are on the bank of the river:

Tosafot on Gittin 60b:10:1.hebrew: במיזל כולי עלמא לא פליגי - אפילו נהר קטן שמימיו פוסקין, כל הרוצה לדלות ידלה, כיון שמושך הנהר כפשטו:
Tosafot on Gittin 60b:10:1.english: When [the water] flows, everyone agrees - Even [in the case of] a small river whose waters cease, anyone who wants to draw [water] may draw, since the river flows in its natural course:

Tosafot on Gittin 60b:13:1.hebrew: והשתא דלא איתמר כו' - לית ליה הא דאמר בפ' יש בכור (בכורות דף מט:): הלכתא כשמואל בדיני וכרב באיסורי; א"נ, הכא מסתבר טעמא דרב, אע"ג דדחקינן מתניתין אליביה:
Tosafot on Gittin 60b:13:1.english: And now that it was not stated, etc. - [Rav Huna bar Taḥalifa] does not hold [of] that which is stated in the chapter [entitled] Yesh Bekhor (Bekhorot 49b): "The halakha is in accordance with Shmuel in monetary matters, and in accordance with Rav in ritual prohibitions." Alternatively, here Rav's reasoning is more plausible, even though we forced the Mishnah [to fit] according to him:

Tosafot on Gittin 60b:15:1.hebrew: כבי תרי עבדת לי - והוא סבר: כיון דאמר "כל דאלים גבר", יכול להערים עליהם. ולא דמי, דמה נפשך מיצעי לא שתו, ואעילאי ותתאי הוא דשייך "כל דאלים גבר":
Tosafot on Gittin 60b:15:1.english: You have acted for me in accordance with two - And he [Rav Shimi bar Ashi] thought: Since [Rav Huna bar Taḥlifa] said, "Whoever is stronger prevails," he could outwit them. But it is not comparable, for either way, the middle [field owners] do not drink [first], and it is [only] to the upper and lower [field owners] that "whoever is stronger prevails" applies:

Tosafot on Gittin 60b:15:2.hebrew: לא טעמינהו - להודיע שלא על פיו עשה, ושמא מכרם, דאין כאן גזל, אלא מפני דרכי שלום בעלמא:
Tosafot on Gittin 60b:15:2.english: He would not taste them - To make known that he [Rav Shimi bar Ashi] did not act upon his [Abaye's] instruction; and perhaps he [Abaye] sold them, since there is no robbery here, rather [it was] merely for the sake of the ways of peace:

Tosafot on Gittin 60b:16:1.hebrew: סליקו נפשייכו מהכא - פי' ר"ח, דלעילאי אמר שאין יכול למחות בהן משום דכל דאלים גבר; וקצת משמע כן, שהרי להן היה מדבר. ומ"מ נראה כפירוש הקונטרס, דלבני חרמך היה מדבר שיסתמו את מסיבתם, ולא דמי לדרב ושמואל כלל:
Tosafot on Gittin 60b:16:1.english: Remove yourselves from here - Rabbeinu Ḥananel explained that [Abaye] said [this] to the upstream [residents] — that [he] cannot prevent them because [the rule is] "whoever is stronger prevails"; and this is somewhat implied, for he was speaking to them. Nevertheless, it appears [correct] according to the explanation of Rashi, that he was speaking to the residents of [Bei] Ḥarmakh, that they should block up their diversion, and it is not at all similar to [the case of] Rav and Shmuel:

Tosafot on Gittin 60b:17:1.hebrew: מצודות חיות ועופות כו' - ולא דמי למרחיקין מצודות הדג מן הדג דפרק לא יחפור (ב"ב דף כא:), דהתם אומנתו בכך ומן הדין הוא שירחיק משם, דא"ל: קא פסקת לחיותי; אבל הכא דאין אומנתו בכך, לא הוי גזל אלא מפני דרכי שלום:
Tosafot on Gittin 60b:17:1.english: Traps of animals and birds, etc. - And [this] is not similar to [the rule that] one must distance fish traps from [another's] fish [traps] in the chapter [entitled] Lo Yaḥpor (Bava Batra 21b), for there, his trade is in that, and by law he must distance [his traps] from there, for he [can] say to him: "You are cutting off my livelihood." But here, where his trade is not in that, it is not robbery except on account of the ways of peace:

Tosafot on Gittin 60b:3:1.hebrew: אתמוהי קא מתמה - במדרש (שמות רבה פ' תשא) אמרינן: "כמו זר נחשבו" — שעובדי כוכבים כתבו את התורה, ואם היה נכתב הכל לישראל, היו עובדי כוכבים הכל כותבין. ולהכי קאמר רחמנא: "אכתוב לו רובי תורה"?! והלא מה שכתבתי להם "כמו זר נחשבו", שהעתיקו זרים. ובקונטרס פירש בענין אחר:
Tosafot on Gittin 60b:3:1.english: [It] is expressing bewilderment - In the Midrash (Shemot Rabbah, Parashat Tissa), we say: "[They] are accounted as a stranger" — for the idolaters wrote the Torah, and if everything had been written for Israel, the idolaters would have written everything. And therefore the Merciful One says: "Should I write for him the greater part of [the] Torah?!" Behold, [even] that which I wrote for them "[is] accounted as a stranger['s]," for strangers copied [it]. And in the Kunteres [Rashi] explained [it] in another way:

Tosafot on Gittin 60b:7:1.hebrew: שיפורא - לפי מה שפי' בקונט' שתוקעין בע"ש, קשה, דבסוף פ' במה מדליקין (שבת דף לה:) משמע דחזן הכנסת היה מניחו בראש הגג; ועוד, דרב יהודה היה בפומבדיתא ורבא במחוזא. אלא נראה כלשון אחר שפירש: שופר שבו נותנין נדבה לתלמידים:
Tosafot on Gittin 60b:7:1.english: Shippura [a horn] - According to what Rashi explained, that they blow [it] on Shabbat eve, [this] is difficult, for at the end of the chapter [entitled] Bameh Madlikin (Shabbat 35b) it is implied that the synagogue attendant would place it on top of the roof; and furthermore, Rav Yehuda was in Pumbedita and Rava was in Mechoza. Rather, it appears like the other explanation that [Rashi] explained: a horn into which they put charity for the students:

Tosafot on Gittin 60b:8:1.hebrew: אלא משום חשדא - פירש ר"ת: שלא יאמרו, מפני החשד שחושדים אותו לגנוב פת של עירוב, אין מניחים אותו שם; אבל בשיפורא ליכא חשדא, שיודעין שמניחים אצל ריש מתיבתא לחלק לתלמידים:
Tosafot on Gittin 60b:8:1.english: Rather, [it is] on account of suspicion - Rabbeinu Tam explained: [This is] so that [people] will not say that because of the suspicion that they suspect him of stealing the bread of the eiruv, they do not place it there. However, regarding the charity box there is no suspicion, for [people] know that they place [it] with the head of the academy to distribute to the students:
